To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‘A combination of high resolution melting analysis (HRM) and simple sequence repeat molecular markers (SSRs) speeds up plum (Prunus salicina and P. domestica) cultivar genotyping and can be successfully applied for the identification of Greek cultivars in an ex situ GeneBank collection.’

(a) HRM is a fast, reliable method for genotyping of plum cultivars, (b) SSRs are useful markers for plum cultivar identification and (c) the combined use of HRM and microsatellites is a fast, cost-effective and efficient method for plum genotyping.
‘HRM analysis combined with SSRs provides a faster, cost-effective and reliable tool for molecular characterization of the Greek plum collection’.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of the genetic resources of Greek plums, as a valuable source of genetic variability for the improvement of this species.

the development of a rapid method for the characterization of plum germplasm collections and the identification of new genotypes, which will be of great importance for breeding programs and for the protection of plant variety rights.
the development and application of a fast, cost-effective method for plum genotyping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HRM analysis combined with SSR markers is a powerful, rapid, and cost-efficient tool for molecular characterization and cultivar identification in plum.
HRM analysis is a powerful tool that could be used in combination with other molecular methods in order to speed up genotyping.

HRM and SSR markers can be used for the characterization of plum genotypes, but HRM is more suitable for the identification of cultivars, while SSRs are useful for the determination of the genetic relationships between the cultivars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this combined method can be used as a fast, reliable and cost-effective tool for the molecular characterization of Prunus germplasm collections.
the HRM method is an effective tool for molecular characterization of Prunus cultivars.
this approach could be a valuable tool for the rapid identification of plum genotypes in germplasm bank collections and breeding programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of HRM analysis with SSR molecular markers can speed up the genotyping of a large number of plum genotypes, which is of great importance for the characterization of germplasm banks and breeding programs.
HRM analysis can be successfully used for molecular characterization of germplasm banks, especially in combination with SSR markers.
HRM can be used as an alternative method to SSRs in the identification of cultivars, and the combination of the two methods can be used to speed up the identification process.
